subject: Dedicated fleet safety factor — Zenfolio throughput & headroom proposal
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Morales <anna@zenfolio.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated fleet safety factor — preliminary numbers and ask

Hi Anna,

Thanks again for the sync this morning. Per our conversation, I've pulled together a concise set of preliminary assumptions for the dedicated capacity proposal so we can validate whether a reserved slab will meet your Q4 traffic targets while preserving latency SLOs. I've attached the traffic profile you shared (zenfolio_traffic_profile_q2.csv) and a short draft mutual action plan.

Summary assumptions (please confirm):
- Peak concurrent inference requests: 3,400 rps at peak marketing campaign windows (14:00–16:00 local)
- Typical request size: 420 tokens input, 160 tokens output → ~580 tokens per request average
- Peak token rate: 3,400 rps * 580 tokens = 1,972,000 tokens/sec peak
- Target p95 generation latency: <= 350ms (end-to-end, model-only p95 target <= 280ms)

Questions for you:
1) Do peak windows ever exceed 3 hours/day or recur across multiple days (holiday traffic)?
2) Any plans to batch client-side requests or shift to async queues for non-interactive flows?

Next steps from our side: Vivek will map tokens/sec → GPU throughput for your preferred model variants and give a recommended slab + safety factor (initial thinking: reserve GPUs to cover steady-state peak + 25–40% safety for burst). We want to align on a safety factor that balances cost predictability and SLA risk.

If that sounds right, we'll follow up with a short capacity worksheet (tokens/sec → effective TPS per GPU for N model variants, assumed KV-cache hit rates, and quantized performance profiles).

Best,
Vanessa

- Peak windows are usually 2–3 hours, but we expect a 6–8 hour elevated period during product launch days (2–3 times/year).
- We will not batch on the client side for web interactions; mobile clients sometimes fall back to an async queue for non-critical tasks.
- We have a hard product requirement that p95 must remain under 400ms for interactive editors.

I'll loop in our infra lead if you need historical logs or additional telemetry. Please proceed with the worksheet.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated fleet safety factor — preliminary numbers and ask

Quick capacity worksheet (high-level) — tagging numbers so we can sanity check with Zenfolio:

Assumptions used:
- Model variant: rw-2.1-large (causal LM) quantized profile (int8) — measured baseline in our lab
- GPU target: H100-80GB (fp16/int8 run)
- Average tokens/request: 580 (confirmed)
- KV-cache hit rate: 28% (conservative; depends on prompt reuse)
- Batch window target to preserve latency: 8–12ms effective batching (continuous batching)

Measured per-GPU effective throughput (tokens/sec) @ p95 <= 280ms model-only:
- rw-2.1-large (int8) on H100-80GB: 175k tokens/sec (single-model steady-state)
- rw-2.1-xl (bigger context/longer seqs): 110k tokens/sec

Mapping peak requirement:
- Peak token demand (from Vanessa): ~1,972,000 tokens/sec
- Using rw-2.1-large: GPUs required (steady) = 1,972,000 / 175,000 ≈ 11.27 → round to 12 GPUs

Safety factor options (examples):
- Conservative (25%): 12 * 1.25 = 15 GPUs (reserve 15)
- Guarded (40%): 12 * 1.40 = 17 GPUs (reserve 17)

Burst strategy suggestions:
- Reserve slab: 12 GPUs as a committed baseline to cover steady-state peak.
- Commit + buffer: recommend reserved 15 GPUs to keep p95 headroom during 2–3x day-of spikes; allow burst up to 20 GPUs from our pooled spare capacity for launch days (billing: committed + metered burst).

Operational considerations impacting numbers:
- If KV-cache hit increases to 45% (better prompt reuse), tokens/sec demand drops ~13% → 10 GPUs steady.
- If you migrate latency-tolerant workloads (image generation / batch exports) to separate tier, the dedicated slab can be smaller.
- Quantization from fp16→int8 shows ~1.5x throughput improvement in our tests but requires verification on your eval prompts (we should run 2–3 representative prompt sets).

Estimated p95 tail risk: with 15 reserved GPUs + 5-GPU burst buffer we expect model-only p95 to remain < 300ms in normal peaks and below 380ms for multi-hour elevated periods; this aligns with your <=400ms product requirement.

Proposed next deliverable: a short two-page "capacity decision matrix" that shows cost delta vs. safety factor (12/15/17 GPUs) and the expected monthly committed cost plus metered burst. I can assemble the matrix and include a sensitivity for KV-cache hit rate (20/30/45%).

Vivek

Anna — thanks for the confirmations and the traffic note on launch days. Vivek's worksheet is exactly what I hoped for.

Proposed mutual action items and timeline:
- Redwood: deliver capacity decision matrix (12/15/17 GPU slabs) + cost projection by EOD Thu 8/2. (Owner: Vivek)
- Zenfolio: share 2 representative prompt sets + one week of request trace (anonymized) for a quick in-house perf run by 8/3. (Owner: Anna)
- Both: agree on safety factor and finalize committed slab by 8/10 to ensure hardware allocation ahead of Q4 campaigns.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_draft.pdf (contains proposed SLAs, billing cadence, and runbook for launch-day burst).
Once we get your prompt sets, we will run two quantization profiles (fp16 and int8) and return measured tokens/sec and p95 numbers so you can choose the optimal cost/perf point. If Zenfolio is comfortable, we can include a one-month trial window for the larger slab to validate during a non-launch elevated day.

Anna — do you want me to route a short purchase order template and the draft MSA (redlines accepted) to your procurement contact after we lock the slab?

Thanks,
Vanessa
